seo.title: Hydraulic Diameter Calculator - Duct Flow
seo.description: Hydraulic Diameter Calculator — Calculate hydraulic diameter for non-circular ducts and pipes used in Reynolds number and pressure drop with instant results & multiple unit support.

formula.explanation: Dh = 4A/P. For rectangular duct: A = W×H, P = 2(W+H). ×1000 converts m to mm.

content.introduction: Hydraulic diameter (Dh = 4A/P) allows using pipe flow equations (Reynolds number, Darcy-Weisbach) for non-circular ducts. For a circular pipe, Dh equals the actual inner diameter.

example.description: 400×200mm rectangular duct: Dh = 267mm, allowing pipe flow equations to be used.

faq.a: Dh lets engineers apply circular pipe correlations (Re, f, Nu) to non-circular geometries like rectangular ducts and annuli.
For an annulus between outer diameter D_o and inner D_i: Dh = D_o − D_i. This calculator handles rectangular ducts.

faq.q: What units should I use for hydraulic diameter?
faq.a: Any consistent length unit works because D_h = 4A/P is a ratio of area to perimeter. Use m with m² and m, or mm with mm² and mm — the result is in the same length unit as the inputs.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Hydraulic Diameter
sections.body:
**Length units**

- 1 m = 1000 mm = 3.28084 ft
- 1 inch = 25.4 mm

**Area units**

- 1 m² = 10.764 ft²
- 1 mm² = 1×10⁻⁶ m²

**Perimeter units**

- Same length unit as the diameter result

D_h = 4A/P is dimensionally consistent: if area is in m² and wetted perimeter in m, D_h is in m. Convert all inputs to the same unit system before computing.
